summary: The Petitioner, **Excel Energy Trading Solution** , a Partnership firm under Section 58(1) of the Partnership Act, 1932, has made the present application under Sections 14 and 15 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) read with Regulation 6 (1) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for the Grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as “the Trading Licence Regulations”), amended from time to time, for the grant of a Category ‘V’ trading licence for inter-State trading in electricity across India. 2. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed for the grant of a Category ‘V’ inter-State Trading Licence and the Petitioner has already complied with all the requirements specified in the Trading Licence Regulations, including the issuance of notice in the Newspapers inviting suggestions/ objections on the present application and prayed to reserve the order in the matter. 3. Vide the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 11.8.2026, the Petitioner was directed to submit the information and clarification regarding: 4. In compliance with the above direction, the Petitioner, vide its affidavit dated (a)The Petitioner has furnished a duly audited Special Balance Sheet as on 31.5.2026, as on the date falling within 30 days immediately preceding the date of filing of the Petition, duly supported by an Independent Auditor’s Report, in accordance with Regulation 3(3)(b) read with Regulation 6(1)(b) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. (c) The Petitioner company confirms that the complete application, along with all annexures and enclosures filed therewith, has been made available on the Petitioner’s website at www.excelpowertrade.net, in compliance with Regulation 6(2) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. (d) The Petitioner company undertakes that it shall not engage in the business of transmission of electricity during the subsistence of the trading licence, if granted by this Commission. 5. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was reserved. _(2) The Applicant shall post complete application along with annexures and enclosures on its website so as to facilitate access to the application by any person through internet and shall keep them on the website till the disposal of the application._ _(4) The Applicant shall within 7 days from the date of publication of the notice as aforesaid submit to the Commission on affidavit the details of the notice published and shall also file the original complete page of the newspaper in which the notice has been published._ _(5) The Applicant shall allow a period of 30 days to the public to file objections or suggestions to the notice of application published in the newspapers._ _(6) The Applicant shall file its reply before the Commission within 30 days from the last date of receipt of objections or suggestions from the public._ _(7) The Commission after consideration of the objections or suggestions received in response to the notice published by the Applicant and its reply may reject the application or may propose to grant licence._ 9. The Petitioner Company, Excel Energy Trading Solution, is a Partnership Firm incorporated under Section 58 (1) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, presently having its business operations from Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Clause 2 of the Partnership Agreement provides that the Petitioner is authorised to undertake trading in electricity. We note that trading in electricity is covered under the Partnership Agreement of the Petitioner. Clause 2 of the Partnership Agreement of the Petitioner company reads as under: - _(a) The parties have mutually agreed to establish and carry on the business of trading in electricity and act as a trader in sale and purchase of electricity and electrical energy in any form and in any marked including power exchange and derivatives market, and by any process and in fuel, derivatives and to enter into demand side management contracts, energy conservation contracts including energy performance contracts, megawatt_ - _(b) To carry on the business of advisory services of Energy Trading and Facilitate Power Trading in the Open Access System or any other system through Intra State and Inter-State Energy Exchange and bilateral trades and act as power trading entity"_ 10. In view of the above, it has been submitted by the Petitioner that it fulfils the requirements specified in Clause (1) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations. 15. In accordance with Clause (2) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations, the Petitioner should have at least one full-time professional possessing qualifications and experience in power system operation and the commercial aspects of power transfer, including finance, commerce and accounts. With regard to full-time professionals, the Petitioner has submitted that (a) Shri Kondaiah Surthani, M.Tech. 16. On consideration of the above facts, after a preliminary examination, we find that the Petitioner meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations for the grant of a Category 'V' trading licence. In view thereof, the Commission proposes to grant a Category 'V' trading licence to the Petitioner. We direct that a notice under Clause (a) of Sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act be issued inviting further suggestions or objections to the proposal of the Commission.
title: Application under Sections 14 and Section 15 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading license and other related matters), Regulations, 2020 for grant of an inter-state trading licence.
